title.narrative: Enhancing Nutrition Services for Under-5s and Pregnant/Breastfeeding Women in Gubio, Yunusari, and Yusufari LGAs, Borno and Yobe States

description.narrative: ltpgtLife at Best Development Initiative (LABDI) proposes a six-month lean season intervention titled " Life-saving preventive and curative nutrition assistance to children under 5 and pregnant breastfeeding women and girls in Borno State and Yobe State" in consortium with Protection without Borders (POWIB). The project aims to reach 10,600 individuals, prioritizing the most vulnerable populations (especially women and children) in three LGAs identified by the Nutrition Sector’s 2025 Multi-Risk Nutrition Emergency Response Preparedness (ERP) Plan as having the highest projected burden of acute malnutrition during the lean season. To ensure sustainability, all nutrition services will be delivered through existing government health facilities. Drawing on LABDI’s extensive experience in Nutrition, WASH, Protection, and Education, the intervention adopts an integrated approach that addresses both the immediate and structural drivers of malnutrition. The project combines the Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM) strategy with protection and livelihoods support to holistically respond to the nutrition crisis. Its core components include IMAM, Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) awareness, as well as Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA). ltbrgtThrough these components, LABDI will deliver high-quality preventive and curative services while building household and community resilience. Specifically, the IMAM component will establish five Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) across Gubio LGA in Borno State as well as Yusufari and Yunusari LGAs respectively in Yobe State to support the early identification and treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition in children under five. MIYCN counselling will empower PBWG and caregivers with knowledge on optimal feeding practices, including exclusive breastfeeding and dietary diversity, aimed at preventing malnutrition. To address immediate nutritional needs, 3,000 severely malnourished children without complications will receive Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF), while 1,500 moderately malnourished children and 300 PBWG will benefit from supplementary feeding. Recognizing the link between nutrition and protection, the project will also conduct GBV and PSEA awareness sessions supported by functional referral systems to ensure survivors receive timely, appropriate care. In addition, CVA will be implemented to provide targeted cash transfers to vulnerable households, increasing their access to nutritious food and supporting adherence to treatment regimens. LABDI partners will work in close collaboration with local health authorities, community leaders, and other stakeholders, and will train twelve health workers and 60 community volunteers to ensure effective delivery of services. By integrating nutrition, protection, and livelihoods, the project addresses the root causes of vulnerability and aligns with the National Multisectoral Plan of Action for Food and Nutrition as well as the Sustainable Development Goals. A comprehensive monitoring and evaluation framework will guide implementation and ensure accountability.ltbrgtTo ensure effective delivery and sustainability, LABDI will strengthen partner capacity through tailored trainings, mentorship, tools, coordination with government systems, and improved data use—enhancing service quality, local ownership, and long-term impact across the three target LGAs.lt/pgt
